statement: unreallabsai/unreal-agent is a single-process, event-loop-coordinated async tool-execution runtime - one goroutine owns a select loop, tool translators run synchronously on it and may not do I/O, work becomes a versioned serializable operation handed to an actor manager, and durability is a versioned append-only session store - so its architecture class is the slot tezgah's hosts occupy, not the slot tezgah occupies.
falsification: A coordinator that runs translators off the loop, an operation value with no Version field, or a store with no Resume and Fork, in the clone at b7c9bf1.

statement: The repository commits an intent before the effect it authorizes: a tool call's status and the operation snapshots it produces are ONE persisted record, the executor is handed operations only from that committed value, and a failed status commit persists nothing, dispatches nothing and starts no request.
falsification: A dispatch path in the clone that hands an operation to the manager before the ToolCallStatus carrying it is persisted, or a fault-injection case that tolerates dispatch-before-commit.

statement: Durable state declares its own format version and a reader refuses by name at record zero: version 1 gets its own message, any other unsupported value gets another, and a control mode the running version no longer models is refused the same way rather than silently reinterpreted.
falsification: A reader that decodes items before checking the header version, or history carrying a removed construct that resumes without a named error.

statement: Input identity comes from the producer and the dedup set is rebuilt from persisted history at startup, so a redelivery after a crash is still a duplicate; the set is seeded from the external input ids the session file carries, and a duplicate is dropped before queueing.
falsification: A seen-set that lives only in process memory, or a dedup path that consults no persisted id on restart.

statement: A delegate may report progress but may not redefine its work: every update returning from the executing party is validated so that the output limit, the operation type and version and the plan bytes are identical to what was handed over, and only a listed status transition is accepted; a handler that stops fails every operation it owned, and two handlers matching one plan is refused rather than picked.
falsification: An update path that accepts a widened output limit, a changed plan, or an unlisted transition, in remote_job_handler.go at b7c9bf1.

statement: Cancellation is its own terminal outcome beside completed and failed, and a late success cannot claim over it: a primitive event that completes after the operation's context is done is rewritten to a canceled event with its result dropped.
falsification: A status vocabulary with no canceled value, or a completed event whose result is accepted after the operation was cancelled.

statement: A shortened text names what it lost and keeps both ends: the bound keeps a head and a tail around a split at half the limit, inserts a marker stating the exact byte count dropped, appends the path of the file holding the complete output when one exists, and stores the untruncated size in a separate field beside the shortened text.

statement: The playbook argues one thing in nine chapters: push the hard invariant down into the layer that can enforce it, so correctness does not depend on every contributor remembering a convention. Its four architecture tests (multiplexed workspace, remote driver, spectator, an automated factory against hostile input) force five consequences - one authoritative session, a trusted control plane, bounded work, explicit compatibility, views as projections - and the session DOM, the Director stack, the component renderer and the TLA+ transcript protocol are each an instance of that single move rather than separate subsystems.

Its conclusion is that documentation would not repair that distribution, so non-replayable state has to be unrepresentable - which is the same defect class this line already recorded against tezgah's own state.json, where phase is author-maintained rather than derived.
falsification: The 78-example review being uncited or its arithmetic self-contradictory, or Appendix A naming failures without linking to the code that produces them.

Its prescription is one central implementation plus an explicit opt-out, not an opt-in helper - and tezgah is the rendering layer, so the rule applies to its injected text directly.
falsification: The document arguing for per-tool truncation, or for an opt-in helper as the target state.

The post is therefore independent evidence for that plan's direction, and it supplies the filtering step the plan does not yet describe.

statement: The post measures what a tool roster costs in wall-clock - a median of 6 runs on a fresh session for task sol gives 36.6s when the roster is limited to five essential tools, against 42.2s and 37.0s for two external references - and concludes that a tool is not a free addition, which is a reason for a stable tiny grammar with the long tail reached through composition rather than for dynamic discovery. tezgah mounts two MCP servers into every session by default and a third opt-in, so the same decision is already made here; this repository's plan 012 is the registry that makes that selection a first-class, persisted choice, and the post supplies the cost the plan does not measure.
falsification: The measurement being absent from the post, or tezgah mounting no MCP server by default so the decision does not exist here.

Nothing in the document commits to keeping those event names and no migration guide is published, so a forward compatibility risk to tezgah's omp adapter follows from the document without any measurement being possible - no successor build was available to test against.
falsification: The document promising that the current extension event names survive, or tezgah's omp support not depending on omp's event names at all.

It states as method six things tezgah already does - derived views over an append-only ledger, a small local model for classification, the long tail behind a stable router, limits enforced at the rendering layer, verification specified in advance, and a declaration that carries its own flags - and it independently validates two plans this repository already has open, 004 on reading recorded failures and 012 on making the optional surface a selection. What is new is one field tezgah's rows lack, a version, and one place its central limit stops short, the cut inside a block; the document's own machinery - session DOM, Director stack, renderer, transcript protocol - presupposes a loop, a session store and a terminal that tezgah does not have.
